subject: English
stem: Which of the following best captures the central argument of the passage?
optA: Traditional parks are being demolished to make way for skyscrapers.
optB: Urban green spaces are evolving from purely aesthetic areas into functional, integrated infrastructure.
optC: Technology has made natural parks unnecessary for city dwellers.
optD: Climate change is the only reason why cities are planting more trees.
solution: The passage opens by saying green spaces were once seen as merely decorative and are now reimagined as living infrastructure that cools cities and absorbs rainwater. That evolution from ornament to function is the central thread. Option A is wrong because the passage never says parks are being demolished for skyscrapers. Matches option B.
context: In many metropolitan areas, the concept of "urban greenery" is undergoing a radical shift. Once viewed merely as decorative patches of grass or formal parks intended for quiet strolls, modern green spaces are being reimagined as "living infrastructure." Today's urban planners are integrating rooftop gardens, vertical forests, and "pocket parks" into the very fabric of skyscrapers and residential blocks. These spaces do more than just provide a visual break from concrete; they act as vital tools for environmental resilience, helping to cool cities through the reduction of the "urban heat island" effect and absorbing excess rainwater to prevent flooding. This transformation is a response to the growing pressures of climate change and rapid urbanization. As city populations swell, the traditional model of large, centralized parks is becoming insufficient. Instead, cities are embracing "biophilic design"---the practice of connecting people with nature within the built environment. From high-tech hydroponic walls in office lobbies to community-led "guerrilla gardening" on abandoned plots, these initiatives reflect a desire to bring nature directly to where people live and work, rather than requiring them to travel to find it. Beyond environmental benefits, these modern green spaces play a crucial role in public health and social cohesion. Research consistently shows that access to nature reduces stress and improves mental well-being. By providing communal areas for urban farming, outdoor exercise, and social gatherings, these spaces help combat the isolation often felt in dense city environments. They serve as "green lungs" that filter air pollution while simultaneously acting as social hubs that bridge the gap between diverse neighborhoods. Ultimately, while the aesthetic of the city is changing, the underlying goal of urban forestry remains constant: to improve the quality of life for inhabitants and ensure that nature remains an essential, accessible part of human existence, even in the heart of a concrete jungle.

subject: English
stem: Convert from direct speech to indirect speech: She said to me, "What can I do for you ?"
optA: She asked me what could she do for me.
optB: She asked me what can she do for me.
optC: She asked me what she could do for me.
optD: She asked me whether she can do anything for me.
solution: A reported wh-question keeps statement word order, so the subject comes before the verb and can becomes could. Options A and B keep the interrogative inversion or the present tense. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Convert from direct speech to indirect speech: He said, 'Alas! I am undone !'
optA: He said that it was his undoing.
optB: He exclaimed pathetically that he was undone.
optC: He stated that he was undone.
optD: He cried that he was being undone.
solution: An exclamation beginning with Alas is reported with a verb of exclaiming plus an adverb of sorrow, and the tense shifts to was undone. The neutral said and stated in the other options lose the exclamatory force. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Convert from direct speech to indirect speech: "I shall unlock the secrets of their success," he said.
optA: He said that he shall unlock the secrets of their success.
optB: He said that he should unlock the secrets of their success.
optC: He said that he would unlock the secrets of their success.
optD: He said that he will unlock the secrets of their success.
solution: In reported speech after a past reporting verb, shall in a first-person statement becomes would. Options A and D keep the present forms shall and will, and should would change the meaning to obligation. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Convert from passive voice to active voice: The purity of justice is maintained by the reports of proceedings in the law courts.
optA: The law courts maintain purity of justice in the reports of the proceedings.
optB: The reports of the proceedings in the law courts maintain the purity of justice.
optC: Pure justice is maintained in the proceedings of the law courts.
optD: The maintenance of justice is pure in the proceedings of the law courts.
solution: The agent in the by-phrase, the reports of the proceedings in the law courts, becomes the subject and the purity of justice becomes the object. Option A wrongly makes the law courts the agent. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Convert from active voice to passive voice: The man put the tea on the slab.
optA: The tea was putted on the slab by the man.
optB: The tea is put on the slab by the man.
optC: The tea has put on the slab by the man.
optD: The tea was put on the slab by the man.
solution: Simple past active becomes was plus the past participle, and the past participle of put is put, not putted. Option B shifts to the present tense and option C is not a passive form at all. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Enervate & Innervate
optA: Enervate means weaken; innervate means supply with nerves
optB: Enervate means to provide more power to someone; innervate means weaken
optC: Enervate means supply with nerves; innervate means paralyse
optD: Enervate means inspire; innervate means irritate
solution: To enervate is to drain of energy or weaken, while to innervate is to supply an organ or tissue with nerves. Option B reverses both senses. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Indict & Indite
optA: Indict means illegally take action; indite means criticise
optB: Indict means formally accuse; indite means compose
optC: Indict means investigate; indite means judge
optD: Indict means accuse someone; indite means record or shoot
solution: To indict is to charge someone formally with a crime, and to indite is to write or compose a piece of writing. Option D gets indict roughly right but glosses indite as record or shoot, which is not a meaning of the word. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Overcome and Succeed
optA: Overcome means triumph over and succeed means to achieve something
optB: Overcome means achieve something and succeed means to triumph over
optC: Overcome means to be successful and succeed means to achieve something
optD: Overcome means winning and succeed means to rise above
solution: Overcome = triumph over an obstacle; succeed = to achieve something desired. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Moot & Mute
optA: Moot means silent; mute means debatable
optB: Moot means irrelevant; mute means silent
optC: Moot means open to debate; mute means silent
optD: Moot means obvious; mute means inactive
solution: Moot means open to argument or debatable, as in a moot point, while mute means silent or unable to speak. Option A simply swaps the two definitions. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Discomfort & Discomfit
optA: Discomfort means embarrassment; discomfit means physical pain
optB: Discomfort means lack of ease; discomfit means baffle
optC: Discomfort means unease; discomfit means relaxation or relief
optD: Discomfort means relief; discomfit means anxiety

subject: English
stem: The young officer's \(\underline{\text{intrepid}}\) behavior during the rescue operation was praised by his superiors.
solution: Intrepid means fearless and bold in the face of danger, which is closest to audacious. Prudent means cautious, the near opposite, and callous means unfeeling rather than brave. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: After years of neglect, the old mansion had fallen into a state of \(\underline{\text{decrepitude}}\).
solution: Decrepitude is the state of being worn out or ruined by age and neglect, which matches dilapidation. Opulence means luxurious wealth, the opposite of what years of neglect produce. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: The diplomat's \(\underline{\text{laconic}}\) reply to the journalist's long question surprised everyone in the room.
solution: Laconic means using very few words, which is succinct, and the contrast with the journalist's long question confirms it. Verbose is the exact opposite. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: It is \(\underline{\text{imperative}}\) for the candidates to carry their original ID proof to the examination hall.
solution: Imperative here means absolutely necessary, which is indispensable. Optional and secondary both weaken the requirement rather than match it. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The sudden \(\underline{\text{plethora}}\) of information on social media often leads to confusion amongmthe public.
solution: A plethora is an excessive amount, that is, an abundance, and only an oversupply would cause the confusion the sentence describes. Scarcity and shortage are antonyms. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: S1. Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance designated under S6. To be listed, a wetland must meet specific criteria, such as supporting vulnerable or endangered species or providing a critical habitat for migratory birds P. These sites are recognized for their significant role in maintaining biodiversity, regulating water cycles, and supporting local livelihoods Q. The Ramsar Convention, an intergovernmental treaty signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran R. Serve as "nature's kidneys" by filtering pollutants from water S. Wetlands act as "biological supermarkets" because they provide a rich food web
solution: S1 ends with designated under, so Q supplying the name of the treaty must follow immediately. P then generalises about the role of these sites, S introduces the biological supermarket image, and R, which has no subject of its own, continues that same description of wetlands. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: S1: In our youth we are apt to think that applause and publicity constitute success. S6: So let us be initiated into the mysteries of maturity and be taught how to resist and spurn the lure of hollow shows. P: The man who values the applause more than his own effort has not outgrown his youth. Q: It is our achievement of work which wins lasting rewards. R: But these are only the trappings, the ephemeral illusions. S: One should concentrate on one's work knowing that applause will come through it.
solution: R begins with But these, referring back to the applause and publicity of S1, so it comes first. Q states what really wins rewards, P criticises the man who values applause more, and S gives the resulting advice, leading naturally into the concluding S6. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: S1- Some old people are oppresse d by the fear of death. S6. Gradually the river grows wider, the banks recede, the waters flow more quietly, and in the end, without any visible break, they becomé merged in the sea and painlessly lose their individual being. P: An individual human existence should be like a river-small at first, narrowly contained within its banks, and rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls. solution: Q refers to this feeling, picking up the fear of death in S1, and R then explains why the young are justified. S turns to the old man with But and prescribes widening one's interests, and P introduces the river image that S6 develops. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: S1: Referent power is a type of soft power. solution: P defines soft power against hard power and S extends that definition to world politics, after which R returns to referent power and Q ends with Think of it as a check-and-balance, which runs straight into the fragment S6 beginning with System. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: S1: Today, philosophers who are interested in figuring out what everything is made of, look to contemporary physics for answers. S6: This kind of research is considered 'philosophy of physics' when done by philosophers and 'foundations of physics' when done by physicists. P: Physicists deftly shift between different pictures of reality as it suits the task at hand. Q: It takes hard work to distil a story about what's really happening in nature from mathematics research. R: The textbooks are written to teach you how to use the mathematical tools of physics most effectively, not to tell you what things the equations are describing. S: But, finding answers in physics is not simply a matter of reading textbooks.
solution: S must follow S1 because But contrasts with looking to physics for answers. P notes that physicists shift between pictures of reality, R explains what textbooks actually do, and Q describes the hard work of distilling a story, which S6 then labels as philosophy of physics. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: You can't be bothered to tell him what you are thinking; ______ he would not listen to you now as he is in a rush.
solution: The blank needs a marker meaning 'regardless' - whatever you say, he would not listen because he is in a rush. 'In any case' carries exactly that concessive force. 'Meanwhile' and 'in the meantime' are time markers, and 'somehow' concerns manner, so none of them fits the relation. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: The project was delayed due to the strike; ______, the budget had already been exhausted.
solution: The exhausted budget is a second, additional problem alongside the strike, so an additive marker is needed. As a result would wrongly make the budget a consequence of the delay. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: ______, I don't think his apology was sincere, even though he said all the right things.
solution: The speaker is offering a frank personal opinion that goes against appearances, which is exactly what To be honest signals. Likewise and On the whole do not fit a first mention of a private doubt. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The team lost the match; ______, they have managed to qualify for the finals based on their overall points.
solution: Losing the match and still qualifying are in contrast, so a concessive marker is required. Hence would wrongly present qualification as a result of losing. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: You can take the shortcut through the park; ______, it might be muddy after last night's rain.
solution: Mind you introduces a cautionary afterthought that qualifies the permission just given, which suits the warning about mud. Although is a subordinating conjunction and cannot stand alone after a semicolon in this slot. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Some people prefer working from home. ______, others find it difficult to stay productive without an office environment.
solution: The two sentences set one group of people against another, which calls for a marker of contrast. In addition and For example would signal continuation or illustration instead. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: ______, the new policy aims to reduce carbon emissions by thirty percent over the next decade.
solution: With no preceding sentence to add to or contradict, only a marker that frames a general statement can open the sentence. What is more and On the contrary both require earlier content to link back to. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: I forgot my wallet at home. ______, could you lend me some change for the bus?
solution: The printed key is 'Incidentally', and the option set is what settles it: 'Consequently' (A) and 'Therefore' (C) are near-synonymous result markers, so if either were intended the item would have two equally correct answers and no unique key. A well-formed item cannot do that, so the intended marker is the one that is NOT a result marker. 'Incidentally' introduces the request as an aside prompted by the situation just mentioned. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Printed key D retained; blind derivation gave A. The blind pass chose 'Consequently' (A) but itself flagged that 'Therefore' (C) is near-synonymous. That observation argues FOR the key rather than against it: if A and C are both valid result markers, neither can be the unique answer of a well-formed MCQ, so the intended answer must be the non-result marker - 'Incidentally' (D). Recorded as a disagreement rather than a correction; the blind answer is not obviously better than the key here. | Possible defect: options A (Consequently) and C (Therefore) are near-synonymous result markers and both read naturally in this blank, so two answers are defensible.

subject: English
stem: The witness provided a detailed account of the accident; ______, the police were able to identify the culprit quickly.
solution: The quick identification is the result of the detailed account, so a consequence marker is required. However and for all that both signal contrast, which the sentence does not contain. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: ______, we must decide whether we want to expand the business or maintain our current size.
solution: 'To sum up' introduces the conclusion a discussion has been leading to - here, the single decision that must now be taken between expanding and holding steady. 'All the same' and 'In any case' both signal concession rather than summary, so neither fits. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Printed key C retained; blind derivation gave B. A usage judgement, not a fact. The sentence poses a decision still to be made ('we must decide whether...'), which suits an opening marker - 'To start with' (B) - better than a closing one. But 'To sum up' (C) is defensible if the sentence is read as closing a prior discussion by naming the decision it leads to. With no preceding context printed, both readings stand.

subject: English
stem: Probity:
optA: The quality of having strong moral principles; honesty and decency
optB: A formal investigation into a person's financial background
optC: The state of being stuck in a difficult or complicated situation
optD: A tendency to be overly critical of others' work
solution: Probity means uprightness and integrity of character. The other options describe a financial audit, a predicament and a critical disposition, none of which is the word's meaning. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Pragmatic:
optA: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically based on practical considerations
optB: Having a tendency to be overly emotional or sentimental
optC: Possessing a great deal of knowledge in a specific scientific field
optD: Being extremely stubborn and refusing to change one's opinion
solution: Pragmatic describes a practical, realistic approach to problems rather than a theoretical or emotional one. Option B describes sentimentality, which is close to the opposite. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Alacrity:
optA: A state of extreme sadness or depression
optB: Brisk and cheerful readiness to do something
optC: The quality of being clear and easy to understand
optD: A loud and confused noise or clamour
solution: Alacrity is eager and cheerful promptness in doing something. Option A gives the opposite mood and option D describes a din. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Quid pro quo:
optA: A person who acts as a middleman in a deal
optB: A legal document that has no official validity
optC: An unexpected turn of events in a court case
optD: Something given or done in return for something else
solution: Quid pro quo is Latin for something for something and denotes a favour or item exchanged for another. The other options describe an intermediary, a void document and a courtroom surprise. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Spurious:
optA: Occurring at irregular intervals; having no set plan
optB: Extremely poisonous or harmful in its effects
optC: Having a sharp or biting taste or smell
optD: Not being what it purports to be; false or fake
solution: Spurious means false or counterfeit, not genuine. Option A defines sporadic and option C defines pungent or acrid. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: P: speed is a potent cause Q: industrial growth at a terrific R: in a big city like Delhi and NCR S: of pollution and numerous diseases
solution: Correct order: 'industrial growth at a terrific (Q) speed is a potent cause (P) of pollution (S) in a big city (R)' = QPSR. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: P: and garbage Q: today our environment R: filth and squalor S: is in constant grip of
solution: Correct order: 'today our environment (Q) is in constant grip of (S) filth and squalor (R) and garbage (P)' = QSRP. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: P: where you don't know the local language Q: and see how your R: travel to a foreign country, even a region of India S: hands and expressions do the talking
solution: R carries the imperative verb and must open, P then adds the relative clause modifying the place, and Q and S complete the second imperative clause about hands and expressions. The full reading is travel to a foreign country, even a region of India, where you do not know the local language, and see how your hands and expressions do the talking. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: P: works of literature Q: inside the pages of all good R: lies the truth about some of S: the more challenging questions posed by humanity
solution: Correct order: Q (inside the pages of all good) -> P (works of literature) -> R (lies the truth about some of) -> S (the more challenging questions posed by humanity). Order: QPRS. Matches option B: QPRS.

subject: English
stem: P: takes on account of its economic successes Q: to address continuing social inequality R: for every stride of progress any nation S: it takes two back if it is unable
solution: Correct order: R (for every stride of progress any nation) -> P (takes on account of its economic successes) -> S (it takes two back if it is unable) -> Q (to address continuing social inequality). Order: RPSQ. Matches option C: RPSQ.

subject: English
stem: The committee was unable to reach a decision as there was a ______ of opinion among the members.
solution: The blank follows the article a and precedes of opinion, so a noun meaning disagreement is required. Different is an adjective, deference means respectful submission and deferment means postponement. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The new government policy is expected to have a significant ______ on the rural economy.
solution: After a significant a noun is needed, and effect is the noun while affect is normally the verb. Effective and affective are adjectives and cannot follow the article here. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Despite being a billionaire, he is known for his ______ lifestyle and simple habits.
solution: Frugal means economical and sparing, which fits the contrast with being a billionaire and pairs naturally with simple habits. Fragile means easily broken, fractious means quarrelsome and fraught means filled with anxiety. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: The lawyer tried to ______ more information from the witness during the cross-examination.
solution: To elicit is to draw out information, which is exactly what a lawyer does in cross-examination. Illicit is an adjective meaning unlawful and cannot follow tried to. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: You must ______ yourself to the changing circumstances if you want to succeed in this job.
solution: To adapt oneself is to adjust to new conditions, which the changing circumstances demand. Adopt means to take up or take in, adept is an adjective meaning skilled and addict does not fit the sense. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: States of Matter, Phase Changes and Diffusion
stem: Which among the following statements is/are incorrect?
optA: The maximum temperature at which a solid melts to become a liquid at the atmospheric pressure is called its melting point.
optB: The melting point of a solid is an indication of the strength of the force of attraction between its particles.
optC: When a solid melts,its temperature remains the same.
optD: The melting point of ice is 273.15 K.
solution: Melting point is simply the temperature at which a solid melts to a liquid at atmospheric pressure; it is not a \(maximum\) temperature, so A is the incorrect statement. B is correct because a stronger interparticle force of attraction requires more energy and therefore a higher melting point. C is correct because the heat supplied during melting is used as latent heat of fusion and the temperature stays constant. D is correct since 0 degrees Celsius equals 273.15 K. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: States of Matter, Phase Changes and Diffusion
stem: Which among the following conditions can liquify gases?
solution: Liquefaction needs the gas particles brought close together and slowed down. Increasing pressure reduces the intermolecular separation and lowering the temperature reduces kinetic energy, so the intermolecular forces can hold the particles together. Hence high pressure with low temperature liquefies a gas. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements: 1.Alloys are mixtures of two or more metals or a metal and a non-metal that can be separated into their components by physical methods. 2.Aerated drinks are gas in liquid solutions. 3.A suspension is formed when solute dissolves completely in the medium. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is false: an alloy is a homogeneous mixture and its components cannot be separated by physical methods. Statement 2 is true: aerated drinks such as soda water are solutions of a gas, carbon dioxide, in a liquid. Statement 3 is false: in a suspension the solute does not dissolve at all but remains as visible dispersed particles; complete dissolution gives a true solution. So only statement 2 is correct. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Types of Reactions: Combination, Decomposition, Displacement
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the types of chemical reactions: 1.Combination reaction involves two or more substances reacting to form a single product. 2.Decomposition reactions require energy in the form of heat,light or electricity. 3.All the double displacement reactions are also redox reactions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is true by definition of a combination reaction. Statement 2 is true: decomposition needs energy supplied as heat, light or electricity, giving thermal, photochemical and electrolytic decomposition. Statement 3 is false: most double displacement reactions, such as precipitation and neutralisation, involve no change in oxidation number and are therefore not redox reactions. So 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Reactivity Series and Reactions with Water
stem: Consider the following statements: 1.Mercury is a good conductor of electricity and heat. 2.Silver is the best conductor of heat. 3.Platinum is the most ductile metal. 4.Lead is a good conductor of heat. How many of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is false as a compound claim: mercury conducts electricity, but the standard textbook statement is that lead and mercury are comparatively poor conductors of heat, so calling mercury a good conductor of heat is wrong. Statement 2 is true: silver is the best conductor of both heat and electricity. Statement 3 is false: gold is the most ductile metal, not platinum. Statement 4 is false for the same reason as statement 1, lead being an explicitly poor conductor of heat. Only statement 2 stands, so exactly one is correct. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Key corrected from B to A. Only statement 2 survives. St.1 and St.4 both fail on the same NCERT Class-10 fact - lead and mercury are comparatively POOR conductors of heat - so 'mercury is a good conductor of electricity and heat' is false as a compound claim and 'lead is a good conductor of heat' is false outright. St.3 is false: gold, not platinum, is the most ductile metal. St.2 is true: silver has the highest thermal conductivity of any metal. One only = A. Corroborated four ways: NCERT text, audited bank row 5da54976 (which keys mercury as a poor thermal conductor), the blind derivation, and an independent re-derivation. The key B most likely counts St.1 on its electrical half while ignoring the heat half.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements: 1. Mixing of an acid with water leads to an increase in H3O+ ions per unit volume. 2. A universal indicator shows different colours at different concentrations of H+ ions. 3. Paper impregnated with a universal indicator can be used for measuring pH. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: mixing an acid with water is dilution, which decreases the number of hydronium ions per unit volume even though the total number of ions is unchanged. Statement 2 is correct: a universal indicator is a blend of dyes that gives a different colour at each hydrogen ion concentration, which is what makes it a pH indicator. Statement 3 is correct: pH paper is exactly paper impregnated with universal indicator. Hence only statement 1 is incorrect. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem: Consider the following reaction: CuO+H2 → Cu + H2O 1.Copper oxide is losing oxygen and is being reduced. 2.Copper is gaining electrons to form atomic copper. 3.Hydrogen is gaining oxygen and is being oxidized. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: In \(\text{CuO} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{Cu} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\), copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced and statement 1 is correct. The copper in \(\text{CuO}\) gains electrons as it is reduced to atomic copper, so statement 2 is correct. Hydrogen gains oxygen to become water, so it is oxidised and statement 3 is correct. All three hold. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following is an example of endothermic reaction?
solution: Slaking of quicklime in A, combustion of carbon in C and combustion of methane in D all release heat and are exothermic. The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate in B needs heat to be supplied continuously to break the compound into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, so it absorbs energy and is endothermic. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Stoichiometry and Laws of Chemical Combination
stem: Consider the following chemical reaction: aFe2O3(s) + bCO(g) → cFe(s) + dCO2 The correct values of a, b, c and d respectively?
solution: Balancing iron first gives 2 atoms of iron on each side, so \(c = 2\) with \(a = 1\). Carbon then requires \(b = d\). Oxygen on the left is \(3 + b\) and on the right is \(2d\), so \(3 + b = 2b\) giving \(b = 3\) and \(d = 3\). Hence a, b, c, d are 1, 3, 2, 3. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem: Which one of the following species is not capable of showing a disproportionation reaction?
solution: Disproportionation needs the element to be in an intermediate oxidation state so that it can be both oxidised and reduced. Chlorine is at \(+1\) in hypochlorite, \(+3\) in chlorite and \(+5\) in chlorate, all of which can be raised further towards \(+7\) and lowered, so all three can disproportionate. In perchlorate chlorine is already at its maximum oxidation state of \(+7\) and cannot be oxidised further, so it cannot disproportionate. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Option A is printed as ClO with the negative charge missing; it is evidently the hypochlorite ion. This does not affect the answer.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements in reference to the trends across the periodic table: 1.The atomic size increases down the group. 2.The atomic radius decreases in moving from left to right along a period. 3.Metallic property increases in moving from left to right along a period. 4.Electronegativity increases down the group. How many of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is true: a new shell is added down a group, so atomic size increases. Statement 2 is true: across a period the nuclear charge rises with no new shell, so the radius decreases. Statement 3 is false: metallic character decreases across a period as electronegativity rises. Statement 4 is false: electronegativity decreases down a group because the valence electrons are further from the nucleus. Exactly two statements are correct. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Consider the following matches: Element Block 1.Magnesium : s block 2.Cobalt : d block 3.Oxygen : f block 4.Uranium : p block How many of the above matches are correct?
solution: Magnesium ends in \(3s^2\) and is an s block element, so match 1 is correct. Cobalt is a first row transition element ending in \(3d^7 4s^2\), so match 2 is correct. Oxygen ends in \(2p^4\) and belongs to the p block, not the f block, so match 3 is wrong. Uranium is an actinide filling the 5f subshell and belongs to the f block, not the p block, so match 4 is wrong. Two matches are correct. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Valency, Oxidation States and Molecular Formula
stem: The valency of phosphorous is:
solution: Phosphorus has the valence configuration \(3s^2 3p^3\), giving three unpaired p electrons and a valency of 3, as in phosphine and phosphorus trichloride. Because it has vacant 3d orbitals it can also promote an electron and use all five valence electrons, giving a valency of 5 as in phosphorus pentachloride. Its valencies are therefore 3 and 5. Matches option D.

subject: Biology
stem: Consider the following matches: Tissue Location 1.Stratified Squamous - Reproductive Epithelium system 2.Columnar epithelium - Stomach 3.Cuboidal epithelium - Oral mucosa Which of the above matches is/are correct?
solution: Match 1 is correct: stratified squamous epithelium lines the skin, buccal cavity, oesophagus and the vagina, so it does occur in the reproductive tract. Match 2 is correct: the lining of the stomach and intestine is simple columnar epithelium, which also secretes and absorbs. Match 3 is wrong: the oral mucosa is stratified squamous, while cuboidal epithelium lines kidney tubules and the ducts of glands. So 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option A.
reviewNote: The first row is garbled in the source, printed as 'Stratified Squamous - Reproductive Epithelium system'; it is read here as stratified squamous epithelium located in the reproductive system.

subject: Biology
stem: Consider the following statements in reference to the Vascular bundles: 1. In the dicotyledonous stem, Cambium is present between phloem and xylem. 2. In the monocotyledonous stem, no cambium is present. 3. The presence of cambium possesses the ability to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues and hence are called closed vascular bundles. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is true: the dicot stem has conjoint bundles with a strip of cambium lying between the outer phloem and the inner xylem. Statement 2 is true: the monocot stem has no cambium, which is why it shows no normal secondary growth. Statement 3 is false: it is the absence of cambium that makes a bundle closed, whereas a bundle containing cambium and able to form secondary xylem and phloem is called an open vascular bundle. So 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option A.

subject: Biology
stem: Consider the following matches between types of RNA and their functions: 1. mRNA : carries amino acids to ribosome 2. tRNA : carries genetic code from DNA ribosome 3. rRNA : provides platform for protein synthesis Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Match 1 is wrong: it is transfer RNA, not messenger RNA, that carries amino acids to the ribosome. Match 2 is wrong for the mirror reason: messenger RNA carries the genetic message transcribed from DNA to the ribosome. Match 3 is correct: ribosomal RNA together with proteins forms the ribosome, which is the structural platform on which polypeptides are assembled. Only statement 3 is correct. Matches option B.

subject: Biology
stem: Consider the following statements in reference to the blood pressure: 1.The pressure in the arteries when the heart is relaxed is diastole. 2.The pressure in the arteries when the heart contracts systole. 3.The systolic pressure is 80mm Hg. Which among the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is true: the arterial pressure during ventricular relaxation is the diastolic pressure. Statement 2 is true: the arterial pressure during ventricular contraction is the systolic pressure. Statement 3 is false: the normal systolic value is about 120 mm Hg, and 80 mm Hg is the diastolic value. So 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option A.

subject: Biology
stem: Consider the following matches in reference to the structure of the heart: Valves Location 1.Pulmonary : between right ventricles and the pulmonary artery 2.Tricuspid : between right atrium and right ventricle 3.Aortic : between the left atrium and the left ventricle 4.Mitral : between the left ventricle and the aorta How many of the above matches is/are correct?
solution: Match 1 is correct: the pulmonary semilunar valve guards the opening from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery. Match 2 is correct: the tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle. Match 3 is wrong: the location given, between the left atrium and the left ventricle, is that of the mitral or bicuspid valve, while the aortic valve lies between the left ventricle and the aorta. Match 4 is wrong by the same swap: the location given, between the left ventricle and the aorta, is that of the aortic valve, not the mitral. Exactly two matches are correct. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Stem repaired. SOURCE TRUNCATION, verified against the raw docx line rather than inferred: the paper prints 'between the left atrium and the left' and stops mid-phrase. 'Ventricle' is the only sensible completion, and it describes the MITRAL valve - which is the point, because statement 4 in turn gives the AORTIC valve's location. The paper has swapped the two descriptions, so both statements are wrong either way and the printed key B ('two only') is correct. This is the minimal repair that completes the sentence and leaves the paper's own key right; the blind derivation independently reached B. | Statement 3 is truncated in the source as 'between the left atrium and the left'; the only sensible completion is 'left ventricle'. Under that reading, statements 3 and 4 carry each other's descriptions, so the Aortic and Mitral entries are swapped and both are wrong, leaving two correct matches. Any other completion of statement 3 also fails to describe the aortic valve, so the count of two is unaffected.

subject: Biology
stem: Which one of the following plant plastids stores starch, oil and protein granules?
solution: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store starch (amyloplasts), oil (elaioplasts), and protein granules. Matches option B: Leucoplast.

subject: Biology
stem: What is the location of intercalary meristem in plants?
optA: Base of the leaves or internodes
solution: Intercalary meristem is the part of the apical meristem that becomes separated from the growing tip by mature tissue, and it persists at the base of leaves or at the internodes, as in grasses. This is why grass regrows after grazing or mowing. Apical meristem occupies the tips of stems and roots, and lateral meristem lies along the sides of stems and roots. Matches option A.

subject: Biology
stem: Mature sclerenchyma cells have:
solution: Sclerenchyma is the mechanical supporting tissue of the plant. Its cells deposit a thick secondary wall impregnated with lignin, the deposition often leaving no lumen, and the protoplast dies at maturity. Mature sclerenchyma cells therefore have lignified walls and are dead. Matches option D.

subject: Biology
stem: Which one of the following organisms does not possess notochord at any stage of its life cycle?
solution: Holothuria, the sea cucumber, is an echinoderm and therefore a non chordate that never develops a notochord. Exocoetus, the flying fish, and the salamander are vertebrates, so both possess a notochord in the embryo. The remaining option is a urochordate, in which the notochord is present in the larval tail. Hence only Holothuria lacks a notochord at every stage. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Option B is printed as 'Hermaduria', which is not a valid genus; it is evidently Herdmania, a urochordate whose larva possesses a notochord. The answer is unaffected.

subject: Biology
stem: Consider the following statements is reference to the fluid mosaic model: 1. It was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972. 2.Carbohydrates are embedded in a lipid bilayer. 3.The phospholipids have hydrophilic heads facing outward and hydrophobic tails facing inwards. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is true: the fluid mosaic model was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972. Statement 2 is false: it is the proteins that are embedded in the lipid bilayer as integral proteins, while carbohydrates occur only as short chains attached to the outer surface in glycoproteins and glycolipids. Statement 3 is true: the bilayer is arranged with the polar hydrophilic heads facing the aqueous surfaces on both sides and the non polar hydrophobic tails turned inward. So 1 and 3 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
optA: Mitosis division leads to the formation of two identical daughter cells, with the same number of chromosomes.
optB: Meiosis occurs in germ cells to produce gametes.
optD: The daughter cells produced after meiosis have double the number of chromosomes than that of mother cells.
solution: The question asks which statement is INCORRECT. Meiosis HALVES the chromosome number - four haploid daughter cells from one diploid parent - so the claim that the daughter cells have double the number of chromosomes is false. The other three are correct: mitosis gives two identical daughter cells, meiosis occurs in germ cells to produce gametes, and it yields four daughter cells. Matches option D.

subject: Biology
stem: Which among the following is the correct sequence of phases of cell division?
solution: The cell first passes through interphase, in which it grows and replicates its DNA, then enters M phase. Within M phase the chromosomes condense in prophase, align on the equator in metaphase, separate to the poles in anaphase and re form nuclei in telophase, after which cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm. Option B wrongly places prophase before interphase, option C reverses anaphase and telophase and option D reverses prophase and metaphase. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: The focal length of a convex lens is 2 m. The power of the lens is
solution: Power of a lens is \(P = 1/f\) with the focal length in metres, so \(P = 1/2 = 0.5\) dioptre. A convex lens is converging, so its focal length and hence its power are taken as positive, giving \(+0.5\) D. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: In Fleming's Right-Hand Rule, the middle finger represents
solution: Fleming's right-hand rule is used to determine the direction of induced current (generator action). Matches option C: induced current.

subject: Physics
stem: One Parsec is approximately equal to
solution: One parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arc second, which works out to about \(3.086 \times 10^{16}\) m. One light-year is about \(9.46 \times 10^{15}\) m, so the ratio is \(3.086/0.946 = 3.26\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following statements for the second law of motion is correct ?
optA: Force is directly proportional to velocity
optB: Force is equal to the rate of change of momentum
optC: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
optD: A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force
solution: Newton's second law states that the net external force on a body equals the rate of change of its linear momentum, \(F = dp/dt\), which reduces to \(F = ma\) for constant mass. Option C is the third law and option D is the first law, while option A is not any of the three laws. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: The temperature of a body increases from 17 °C to 42 °C. The increase in temperature expressed in kelvin is
solution: The rise on the Celsius scale is \(42 - 17 = 25\) degrees. A kelvin and a Celsius degree are the same size, since \(T_K = t_C + 273.15\) and the constant cancels in a difference: \((42 + 273.15) - (17 + 273.15) = 25\) K. The offset of 273 applies to a temperature reading, not to a temperature INCREASE, so 290 K and 315 K are the two absolute readings and not the answer. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: The direction of gravitational field at a point is
optA: Away from the mass producing it
solution: Gravitational field is the force per unit mass on a test mass, and gravitation is always attractive, so the field at any point points towards the mass producing it. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: The SI unit of atmospheric pressure is
solution: All four options are units of pressure, so the discriminator is which one belongs to SI. The SI unit is the pascal, defined as one newton per square metre; dyne per square centimetre is CGS, while bar and atmosphere are accepted non-SI practical units. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Compared to the primary rainbow, the secondary rainbow is
solution: The primary rainbow is produced by one total internal reflection inside each raindrop and the secondary by two, and light escapes at every reflection, so the secondary is fainter. The extra reflection also shifts the emerging cone outwards, from about 40 to 42 degrees for the primary to about 50 to 53 degrees for the secondary, so the secondary arc is larger and lies outside the primary with its colour order reversed. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: The height of a geostationary satellite above the Earth's surface is approximately
solution: A geostationary satellite must have a period of 24 hours, which by Kepler's third law fixes the orbital radius at about 42400 km from the Earth's centre. Subtracting the Earth's radius of about 6400 km leaves a height of roughly 36000 km above the surface. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: A man carrying a bag of mass 30 kg is moving with a speed of 2 m/s. If the mass of the bag is reduced to 15 kg while moving and no external force acts on the system, what will be the new speed according to the law of conservation of momentum?
solution: Taking the intended reading that the moving load alone is the system and that its momentum is conserved, the initial momentum is \(p = 30 \times 2 = 60\) kg m/s. With the mass reduced to 15 kg the same momentum gives \(v = 60/15 = 4\) m/s, so halving the mass doubles the speed. Matches option B.
reviewNote: The question is physically defective. Mass cannot simply vanish from an isolated system: if half the load is released it carries its own momentum away at 2 m/s, and the remainder continues unchanged at 2 m/s (option C), which is the physically correct outcome. The stem also never gives the man's mass, so the system it names (man plus bag) is underspecified and no numerical answer follows from it. Only the naive reading p = mv with m halved yields 4 m/s.

subject: Physics
stem: Work done by a force is negative when the angle between force and displacement is
solution: Work \(W = F \cdot S \cos\theta\). Negative work occurs when \(\theta = 180°\) (anti-parallel), giving \(\cos 180° = -1\), so \(W = -FS\). Matches option C: anti-parallel to each other.

subject: Physics
stem: A car travels one-third of a journey with speed 30 km/h and the remaining journey with speed 60 km/h. The average velocity of the car is:
solution: Let the total distance be \(d\). The first leg takes \(t_1 = (d/3)/30 = d/90\) and the second leg takes \(t_2 = (2d/3)/60 = 2d/180 = d/90\), so the total time is \(2d/90 = d/45\). The average speed is therefore \(d \div (d/45) = 45\) km/h. The two legs happen to take equal times here, which is why the weighted result coincides with the plain mean of 30 and 60; the mean is not the method. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A satellite revolves around a planet in 16 hours. If the radius of its orbit is doubled, the new time period will be:
solution: Kepler's third law gives \(T^2 \propto R^3\), so \(T_2/T_1 = (R_2/R_1)^{3/2} = 2^{3/2} = 2.8284\). Hence \(T_2 = 16 \times 2.8284 = 45.25\) hours. Doubling the radius does not double the period, so 32 h and 64 h are both wrong. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: For a body falling freely from rest, which of the following statements is correct?
optA: Both kinetic and potential energies increase
optB: Both kinetic and potential energies decrease
optC: Kinetic energy increases while potential energy decreases
optD: Both kinetic and potential energies remain constant
solution: As the body falls its height decreases so gravitational potential energy \(mgh\) decreases, while its speed increases so kinetic energy \(\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) increases. In the absence of air resistance the sum stays constant, the loss in potential energy exactly appearing as kinetic energy. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A body is projected vertically upward with speed 20 m/s. The average speed during the complete journey is
solution: Taking \(g = 10\) m/s squared, the rise takes \(t = u/g = 20/10 = 2\) s and the maximum height is \(h = u^2/2g = 400/20 = 20\) m. The complete journey covers a path length of \(2h = 40\) m in a total time of 4 s, so the average SPEED is \(40/4 = 10\) m/s. In general the answer is \(u/2\) and is independent of \(g\); the average VELOCITY over the same trip is zero because the displacement is zero, which is the trap in option A. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Key corrected from A to D. The stem asks for average SPEED. Total path length = 2 x u^2/(2g) = 40 m over a total time of 2u/g = 4 s, giving 10 m/s = option D. In general the answer is u/2, independent of g. Option A (0 m/s) is the average VELOCITY, which is zero because the displacement is zero - the setter keyed the distractor the question was built to test. Blind derivation reached D at HIGH confidence; independently re-derived.

subject: Physics
stem: For a particle in uniform circular motion, the acceleration is
optC: Constant in magnitude but changing in direction
optD: Changing in both magnitude and direction
solution: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, so the centripetal acceleration \(a = v^2/r\) has a fixed magnitude, but it always points towards the centre and that direction turns continuously as the particle moves. The acceleration is therefore non-zero and constant in magnitude while changing in direction. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following physical quantities is not dimensionless?
solution: Mach number is a ratio of two speeds, refractive index a ratio of two speeds of light, and relative density a ratio of two densities, so all three are pure numbers. Stress is force per unit area with dimensions \([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\) and the SI unit pascal, so it is not dimensionless. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: Why is it easier to pull a cart than to push it?
optA: Less force is applied while pulling
optB: Pulling reduces the normal reaction and hence friction reduces
optC: Friction is independent of normal reaction
solution: When the cart is pulled at an angle the applied force has an upward vertical component, so the normal reaction becomes \(N = mg - F\sin\theta\); when it is pushed the vertical component presses down and \(N = mg + F\sin\theta\). Since friction is \(f = \mu N\), pulling gives the smaller normal reaction and hence the smaller opposing friction. The weight itself is unchanged, so option D is wrong. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A force of 5 N acts on a body and displaces it by 4 m opposite to the direction of force in 2 s. The power developed is
solution: The displacement is opposite to the force, so the angle between them is 180 degrees and \(W = Fs\cos 180 = -5 \times 4 = -20\) J. Power is work per unit time, \(P = -20/2 = -10\) W. The negative sign says the force removes energy from the body rather than supplying it. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: The force of friction between two surfaces does not depend on
optA: Area of contact between the surfaces
optB: Nature of the surfaces in contact
solution: The laws of friction state that \(f = \mu N\), so friction depends on the nature and roughness of the surfaces through \(\mu\) and on the mass through the normal reaction \(N = mg\). It is independent of the apparent area of contact, because increasing the area reduces the pressure proportionally and leaves the true contact area unchanged. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A body is projected horizontally from the top of a cliff of height 20 m with a speed of 15 m/s. The horizontal range of the body is:
solution: For horizontal projection the vertical motion starts from rest, so \(h = \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2\) gives \(t = \sqrt{2h/g} = \sqrt{40/10} = 2\) s. The horizontal velocity is unchanged, so the range is \(R = ut = 15 \times 2 = 30\) m (with \(g = 9.8\) the value is 30.3 m, still 30 m). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: Impulse of a force is numerically equal to the:
solution: Impulse is defined as \(J = F\Delta t\), and by Newton's second law \(F = \Delta p/\Delta t\), so \(J = \Delta p\). This is the impulse-momentum theorem, and both quantities share the unit newton second. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Two satellites of masses m and 4m revolve around the Earth in the same circular orbit.The ratio of their orbital velocities is:
solution: Equating gravitational force to the centripetal requirement, \(GMm/r^2 = mv^2/r\), the satellite mass \(m\) cancels and \(v = \sqrt{GM/r}\). Orbital speed therefore depends only on the central mass and the orbital radius, so two satellites in the SAME orbit have the same speed whatever their masses, giving a ratio of 1:1. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Which type of mirror is used by ENT doctors for examining ears and throat?
solution: ENT specialists use a concave mirror with a central aperture as a head mirror, because a concave mirror converges the light from a lamp onto a small area and so illuminates the ear, nose or throat brightly. It also gives an enlarged erect virtual image when the part examined lies within its focal length. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: In a solar cell, the energy conversion is
solution: A solar cell is a photovoltaic device: incident light (photon) energy is converted directly into electrical energy. It is not a thermal, chemical or mechanical converter, which rules out the other three. Matches option B.

subject: Economics
stem: The headquarters of International, Monetary Fund is located at:
solution: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered at 700 19th Street NW, Washington D.C., in the United States of America, alongside its Bretton Woods sibling the World Bank. Switzerland (Geneva/Basel) hosts the WTO, WHO and BIS but not the IMF. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Energy and Industries — Power, Petroleum, Iron and Steel
stem: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists : List-I (Power Plant) List-II (State) A. Satpura 1. Maharashtra B. Dhuvaran 2. Uttarakhand C. Tanakpur 3. Gujarat D. Dabhol 4. Madhya Pradesh Code: A B C D
solution: Working the pairs individually: Satpura Thermal Power Station is at Sarni in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh (4); Dhuvaran Thermal Power Station is in Anand district, Gujarat (3); the Tanakpur hydroelectric project is on the Sharda river in Champawat district, Uttarakhand (2); and the Dabhol (Ratnagiri) gas-based plant is in Maharashtra (1). This gives A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport

stem: Which one among the following is NOT a beneficiary state from the Vindhyachal Power Plant of the NTPC ?
solution: Vindhyachal Super Thermal Power Plant (MP) primarily supplies to MP, UP, Rajasthan and central/northern states. Goa is not a beneficiary. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: The international dispute about modern environmental movement began with the publication of Silent Spring by
solution: Silent Spring (1962) was written by the American marine biologist Rachel Carson, and its indictment of indiscriminate pesticide use, especially DDT, is conventionally credited with launching the modern environmental movement. Mary Daly, Carolyn Merchant and Maria Mies are ecofeminist writers of a later generation. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: What is the nickname of the Men's Cricket team of Zimbabwe ?
solution: Zimbabwe's men's cricket team is nicknamed The Chevrons, after the chevron pattern on the team crest and kit. The Kangaroos and The Kookaburras are Australian sporting nicknames and The Boomers is Australia's men's basketball team. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Lapland is a cultural region largely within the Arctic Circle in the north of the Scandinavian peninsula.Who inhabited Lapland ?
solution: Lapland, spanning northern Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola peninsula of Russia, is the homeland of the Sami, an indigenous reindeer-herding people. The Padaung are of Myanmar, and the Hamar and Himba are African peoples of Ethiopia and Namibia respectively. Matches option A.

chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: State of Manipur shares borders with how many other countries and Indian states respectively ?
solution: Manipur has an international boundary with only one country, Myanmar, on its east and south-east. Domestically it touches three Indian states: Nagaland to the north, Assam to the west and Mizoram to the south-west. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following river basins is located to the southernmost ?
solution: Ordering the four basins from north to south gives Tapi (about 21 degrees north), Godavari (about 19 degrees north), Krishna (about 16 degrees north) and Kaveri (about 11 to 12 degrees north). The Kaveri basin, draining Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, is therefore the southernmost. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following is/are cold ocean current(s) ? 1. Alaska Current 2. Agulhas Current 3. Falkland Current 4. West Australian Current Select the answer using the code given below :
solution: The question asks for the COLD currents. The Falkland Current (flowing north along south-eastern South America) and the West Australian Current (flowing north along western Australia) are both cold. The Alaska Current and the Agulhas Current are warm, so statements 1 and 2 are excluded. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Siachen Glacier is situated to the:
solution: The Siachen Glacier lies in the eastern Karakoram immediately north of the Nubra valley, which carries its meltwater into the Shyok. Aksai Chin lies far to its east and Gilgit far to its west, while Leh is well to the south, so the other three descriptions are all misdirected. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: Spruce and cedar are tree varieties of
solution: Spruce and cedar are conifers characteristic of temperate coniferous forests. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: Consider the following places of india 1.Itanagar 2.Imphal 3.Agartala 4.Aizwal Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the above places in terms of sunrise time?
solution: Sunrise reaches the EASTERNMOST place first (the Earth spins west to east), so order the places by longitude, east to west. Longitudes: Imphal ~93.9E (2), Itanagar ~93.6E (1), Aizawl ~92.7E (4), Agartala ~91.3E (3). Chronological order of sunrise = Imphal, Itanagar, Aizawl, Agartala = 2-1-4-3 = option (B). The recorded/official key is (C) 1-4-3-2, which places Imphal last despite it being the easternmost — preserved here as the official answer, but flag the discrepancy: by longitude the order should begin with Imphal.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: Which one among the following is the nearest from the 'Zero Mile Centre' of India?
solution: The Zero Mile Stone, the notional geographic centre from which colonial distances in India were measured, stands at Nagpur in Maharashtra. Straight-line distances from Nagpur are roughly 500 km to Hyderabad (Charminar), 700 km to Mumbai (Gateway of India), 900 km to Agra (Taj Mahal) and 1100 km to Kolkata (Victoria Memorial), so the Charminar is nearest. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
chapter: National Events, Persons and India General Knowledge
stem: Which Country Has the Largest Number of Paid Newspapers in the World ?
solution: India has the largest number of paid-for daily newspaper titles in the world, a position it has held in successive World Association of Newspapers surveys, because its press is fragmented across many languages and regional editions. China leads on aggregate circulation of individual titles but not on the number of paid titles. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following factors do not influence the ocean currents ? 1. Coriolis force 2. Gravity 3. Heating by solar energy 4. Wind Select the answer using the code given below :
solution: All four factors influence ocean currents: Coriolis force (deflects currents), gravity (thermohaline), solar heating (density differences), and wind (surface currents). Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
stem: Which of the following cities are Not Situated along the Persian Gulf ? 1.Doha 2.Dubai 3.Jeddah 4.Yanbu Select The correct answer using the code given Below
solution: Doha in Qatar and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates both stand on the Persian Gulf, so 1 and 2 are not the answer. Jeddah and Yanbu are both Saudi Arabian ports on the Red Sea coast on the opposite side of the Arabian peninsula, so it is 3 and 4 that are not on the Persian Gulf. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
stem: The Suez canal, the Strait of Hormuz and the Strait of Gibraltar Are important because they
optB: Prohibit The movement of ships carrying Nuclear weapons
optC: Unite Russian access to warm water points
optD: Control access to vital trade routes
solution: All three are chokepoints: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, Hormuz is the only sea outlet from the Persian Gulf, and Gibraltar is the sole entrance to the Mediterranean from the Atlantic. Their strategic value lies precisely in controlling access to heavily used trade and oil routes, not in preventing attacks or barring particular cargoes. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem: Which of the following are called the "ports of call" ?
optA: These ports have only strategic importance
optB: Ports where goods are brought for export from different countries
optC: Ports where ships used to anchor for refuelling
optD: Ports which are exclusively concerned with transportation of passengers
solution: Ports of call are those that originally developed as staging points on long ocean routes where ships halted to take on fuel, fresh water and provisions, such as Aden, Honolulu and Singapore. Ports handling export cargo from a hinterland are entrepot or commercial ports, and passenger-only harbours are packet stations. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem: Which one among the following Union Territories of India shares the shortest length of National Highways?
solution: In the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways statistics the National Highway length in Chandigarh is only about 15 km, against roughly 22 km in Daman and Diu, 31 km in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and 80 km in Delhi. Chandigarh therefore carries the shortest National Highway length of the four Union Territories listed. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Chandigarh and Daman and Diu are close (about 15 km against about 22 km) and different published editions of the road statistics vary by a few kilometres, so this item turns on which year's data the setter used.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Avatar,Actuators, and Gynoids, are all forms of
solution: A gynoid is a humanoid robot built in female form, an actuator is the motor or drive element that produces a robot's movement, and an avatar in robotics is a telepresence humanoid controlled remotely by an operator. All three belong to the vocabulary of humanoid robotics rather than to cryptocurrency, startups or medical apps. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
